description: Total collapse of a national road bridge on the SS647 Bifernina near Campobasso (Molise) on 25 January 2000, triggered by hydraulic forces during winter rainfall causing the Biferno river to flood. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Piena documentata; meccanismo di dettaglio non ricostruibile dalle fonti disponibili.

Partial collapse / severe damage of a road bridge over the Po at Crissolo during the 13–16 October 2000 flood. The official ARPA Piemonte event report documents irreversible damage to a stone-arch bridge in the municipality and several Po crossings upstream destroyed or severely damaged. The exact identity and detailed failure mechanism of this database record cannot be uniquely reconstructed; process and component therefore remain Unspecified.

Partial collapse of a road bridge over the Po near Crissolo during the October 2000 flood. D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P008, classifies the process as lateral bank/embankment erosion with damage involving abutment/superstructure components. The official ARPA Piemonte report independently documents severe bridge damage and destroyed crossings along the Po in the Crissolo area.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Stura di Ala near Ala di Stura (Torino) on 13-16 October 2000, as part of the catastrophic alluvione. Documented in the ARPA Piemonte official report (Valle di Viù area). Total collapse during the catastrophic alluvione of 13-16 October 2000 that struck over 50% of Piemonte, causing more than 1,800 documented damage events. The ARPA Piemonte report (2003) explicitly documents multiple bridge collapses across the Stura di Lanzo, Orco, Chisone, Dora Riparia, Dora Baltea and Po basins. The event is comparable in scale to the 1994 alluvione del Piemonte. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse. Piena documentata; meccanismo di dettaglio non ricostruibile dalle fonti disponibili.

Total collapse of the provincial road bridge over the Trigno river connecting Montenero di Bisaccia (Campobasso, Molise) with San Salvo (Chieti, Abruzzo) on 25 January 2003 at 12:58, triggered by the catastrophic flooding of the Trigno during a violent three-day alluvione. The fifth pier gave way in front of a crowd of onlookers, cutting the main road connection between Molise and Abruzzo for months. A temporary bailey bridge was opened in June 2003 as an emergency measure but suffered repeated flooding closures. Reconstruction began in December 2005 following prolonged bureaucratic delays between the provinces of Campobasso and Chieti. The new permanent bridge was inaugurated in December 2006. No fatalities or injuries were reported from this collapse. The same bridge structure collapsed again during the April 2026 Molise flood event. ATTENZIONE: le coordinate della scheda distano ~250 km dalla posizione reale del ponte (41.778, 14.571 nel DB Polimi): correggere latitudine/longitudine.

The collapse isolated the fraction of Pietratagliata for days. The broader event caused 2 deaths (Gerti Schnabl in Ugovizza, Bruno Urli in Malborghetto) and mobilised 2,687 civil protection volunteers. Reconstruction of the bridge and the SS13 access road required 6 years and €13.4 million. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse. The broader event killed two people (Cosimo Filiberto Fanelli and Domenico Quarato) and caused €28 million of damage in Palagiano alone. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific bridge collapse. The bridge was subsequently rebuilt but collapsed again during the October 2005 flood (B05.10.01), requiring a second reconstruction project managed by PPV Consulting. Citato nella letteratura tecnica (Convegno FABRE 2022) tra i crolli per scalzamento di pile in alveo.

Total collapse of a national road bridge over the Taloro river near Nuoro (Sardinia) on 8 December 2004, triggered by hydraulic forces during the severe autumn flooding that struck central Sardinia. Total collapse of the Ponte Chiavalir on the SR552 (Strada Regionale 552 del Passo Rest) over the torrente Vielia at Tramonti di Sopra (Pordenone, Friuli-Venezia Giulia) on 15 December 2004 at approximately 10:00, during a static load test (collaudo statico) one hour before the official commissioning ceremony. Three trucks loaded with gravel were placed on the 30-metre span to verify its structural capacity; the bridge bent into a V-shape and all three trucks fell into the Vielia stream. Driver Angelo Picotto (75, Mortegliano) was trapped in his cab and sustained non-serious injuries; the other two drivers escaped. Expert investigation attributed the collapse to missing bolts and irregularities in construction execution. In December 2011, the Cassazione confirmed convictions for 4 of 6 defendants: designer Michele Artusato (1 year), site manager Franco Fusciello (8 months), builders Walter Ortolan and Domenico Bruno (1 year 4 months), and surveyor Vigilio Ciriani (1 year). The DB lists municipality as Tramonti di Sotto — corrected to Tramonti di Sopra based on all sources.

Total collapse of a national road bridge over the Oglio river on the SS42 del Tonale e della Mendola near Capo di Ponte (Brescia, Lombardy) on 27 June 2005. One person was killed and four were injured when the bridge structure failed. The collapse was attributed to design and construction defects. Capo di Ponte is a municipality in Val Camonica whose name derives from its historical position at the head of a bridge over the Oglio river; the SS42 is the main valley artery connecting the Brescia plain with the Alpine passes. The Procura di Brescia opened an investigation.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over a valley (gravina) in the municipality of Massafra (Taranto, Apulia) on 8 October 2005, triggered by hydraulic forces during the intense autumn rainfall that struck the Taranto area. Five people were killed when their vehicles crossed or were near the bridge as it gave way. Two additional people were injured. The collapse occurred the night before the Eurostar 9410 train derailment (24 October 2005, 35 injured), both caused by the same exceptional meteorological event described by Protezione Civile president Guido Bertolaso as an 'exceptional climate event.' A car was also swept into the sea in Bari city during the same event, killing one more person. The broader event caused at least 7 deaths across Apulia. Total collapse of the Ponte di Carasco over the torrente Sturla (Valfontanabuona, Genova, Liguria) on 22 October 2013 during a violent flash flood (nubifragio) that struck the Fontanabuona valley. Two people died — Gino Gattorna (68) and Claudio Rosasco (45), both from Moconesi — whose car was swept into the flooded Sturla as the bridge collapsed while they were crossing. The bridge was a 55-metre national road crossing on the SP 225 Fontanabuona. One further person was injured. Subsequent judicial proceedings saw 4 employees of the former Provincia di Genova charged with culpable homicide and culpable collapse (allegedly prolonged failure to carry out scheduled inspections); they were acquitted in May 2017. The bridge was rebuilt in exceptional time — completed in 6 months — and reopened in April 2014. Consulenza idrologico-idraulica (Studio Majone): scalzamento al piede della pila sinistra durante la piena dello Sturla (T~50 anni), aggravato da difformita' degli interventi 1978 sulle due pile.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Padrongianus river near Olbia (Sassari, Sardinia) on 18 November 2013, triggered by the catastrophic flooding caused by Ciclone Cleopatra — which dropped 440 mm in a few hours, killing 19 people across Sardinia and causing €660 million of damage. Olbia suffered 9 deaths. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse. Total collapse of the Ponte di Oloè on the SP46 provincial road between Oliena and Dorgali (Nuoro, Sardinia) on 18 November 2013, caused by the catastrophic flooding of the Cedrino river during Ciclone Cleopatra. Inspector Luca Tanzi (40), a police officer responding to the emergency with three colleagues escorting an ambulance, was killed when the bridge spalletta collapsed suddenly at approximately 18:30, plunging his Land Rover into the void. His three colleagues survived. The bridge was placed under judicial sequestration; subsequent works were found to use substandard materials. A 30-person trial for culpable homicide and disastro colposo was opened; a second trial addressed the fraudulent reconstruction. The bridge was not reopened for over 10 years. Cedimento del terrapieno/rilevato in corrispondenza del ponte durante la piena del Cedrino (ciclone Cleopatra); il vecchio rilevato ostruiva il deflusso (fonte ANSA/Regione Sardegna).

Total collapse of a section of the SP38 provincial road at Monte Pino near Olbia (Sassari, Sardinia) on 18 November 2013, caused by a voragine (sinkhole/collapse) triggered by the catastrophic flooding of the Rio Badu Pinasu stream during Ciclone Cleopatra. Three people died: Bruno Fiore, his wife Sebastiana Brundu, and his consuocera Maria Loriga, who were travelling on the road when a large section gave way. The collapse created a monument to 'inefficiency' — the road remained unrepaired for years. Three people were convicted by the Tribunale di Tempio Pausania in March 2022 for culpable collapse and culpable homicide. Piano degli interventi ex OCDPC 122/2013, Commissario delegato emergenza alluvione Sardegna (All. A Ordinanza commissariale n. 23 del 23/01/2014), Allegato 2, scheda ID 26 (Provincia Olbia-Tempio, SP 38 - Monte Pino): "Crollo di un tratto di rilevato lungo circa 20 m in corrispondenza dell'opera idraulica, per probabile erosione del materiale di riporto ai fianchi del tubolare di cemento armato dovuto all'eccezionalita' della piena". Meccanismo: cedimento del rilevato stradale sovrastante il tombino/tubolare in c.a., per erosione del riporto (la scheda tecnica qualifica essa stessa l'erosione come "probabile"). Nota: la scheda attribuisce il sito al comune di Telti (Monte Pino ricade al confine Telti/Olbia), mentre il DB riporta Olbia; localita' e strada coincidono. [Il database Polimi (D'Angelo et al. 2025, S3, record P073, dec=0.5) classifica invece il processo come: altro processo (es. colata detritica/frana).]

Total collapse of a second provincial/regional bridge over the Cedrino river near Oliena (Nuoro, Sardinia) on 18 November 2013, caused by Ciclone Cleopatra. Partial collapse of the Viadotto Navicelli, a moveable road bridge on the FiPiLi superstrada at Calambrone (Pisa, Tuscany) crossing the Canale dei Navicelli, on 23 April 2014 at approximately 11:00. During a closing manoeuvre after allowing a sailing vessel to pass, a series of bridge components fell onto the roadway below, causing panic among motorists. The collapse was caused by the failure of bolts holding the moveable span. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The bridge, managed by Società Navicelli, is a vital link between the Pisa and Livorno nautical industrial districts; its closure severely disrupted operations for dozens of nautical firms. Repairs required at least one month and two cranes. Confindustria noted that an analogous collapse had occurred at the same bridge in 2014 when a further event occurred in 2026. Progetto del 1990 (ramo livornese FI-PI-LI, piano 'Italia '90'), ANAS stazione appaltante, collaudato nel 2004; ponte mobile levatoio sul canale dei Navicelli. NB: un secondo, distinto collasso ha interessato lo stesso ponte il 06/03/2026 per rottura di una delle due cerniere in acciaio del meccanismo di sollevamento (non idraulico): valutare se aggiungere come scheda separata.

Total collapse of a span of the Viadotto Petrulla on the SS626 national road in the contrada Petrulla, territory of Licata (Agrigento, Sicily) on 7 July 2014. The bridge deck collapsed downward from a height of approximately 4 metres due to sudden failure of the prestressed concrete carrying beams, splintering at mid-span. Two vehicles were involved in the incident: four people sustained minor injuries, including a pregnant woman who was airlifted to hospital in Caltanissetta as a precaution. ANAS immediately established an internal investigation commission. The Procura di Agrigento opened a criminal investigation. The event was subsequently cited by CNR-ITC as a significant example of prestressed concrete failure in Italian bridge infrastructure, comparable to the later Fossano (2017) collapse.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the SS3 Via Flaminia national road near Rome (Lazio) on 24 July 2014, caused by the impact of a heavy goods vehicle with an oversized load that struck the underside of the bridge while travelling on the road below. Total collapse of the Viadotto Scorciavacche on the SS189 Palermo-Agrigento expressway near Mezzojuso (Palermo, Sicily) on 30 December 2014, exactly seven days after its inauguration. The viaduct had been opened without the required structural testing and certification (collaudo), with ANAS having moved the inauguration forward by three months. The structure, built on unstable terrain, failed within a week of opening to traffic. The collapse was a major national scandal: Prime Minister Matteo Renzi expressed public outrage; the Procura di Termini Imerese opened an investigation for attentato alla sicurezza dei trasporti and falso, indicting the ex-ANAS president Pietro Ciucci and several ANAS directors. After years of procedural battles, most charges were declared prescribed in 2023; in January 2025 the remaining defendants were acquitted. No fatalities or injuries were reported as the viaduct failed without vehicles in transit.

Total collapse of approach span no. 13 (Reggio Calabria side) of the Viadotto Italia on the A3/A2 del Mediterraneo motorway between Laino Borgo and Mormanno (Cosenza, Calabria) on 2 March 2015 at approximately 17:00, during demolition works as part of the Macrolotto 3.2 motorway widening programme. The steel span, found to lack fixings on both supports, slid off pier 12 and fell approximately 80 metres into the Lao gorge below. One worker — Adrian Ionel Miholca, 25, Romanian national of Nitrex Srl — was carried down with the span and died on impact. The Procura di Castrovillari sequestered the entire viaduct; the A3 between Laino Borgo and Mormanno remained closed for several months, effectively isolating Calabria from the rest of Italy along the main north-south motorway axis. ANAS established an internal inquiry commission. The Viadotto Italia, designed with consultancy of Riccardo Morandi and inaugurated in 1969, was at the time the highest bridge in Italy (240m above the valley floor) and had been Europe's highest until 2004.

Partial collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Cerami river near Cerami (Enna, Sicily) on 14 March 2015, caused by structural deterioration in the absence of adequate maintenance. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Cerami has a notable medieval arch bridge of the XII century over the Cerami river, but this event relates to a separate structure in the same area. Limited documentation available for this specific event.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge on the panoramic road of Enna (Sicily) on 28 March 2015, triggered by hydraulic phenomena during spring rainfall. Total collapse and severe deformation of the Himera motorway viaduct near Scillato (Sicily) on 10 April 2015 caused by a large landslide affecting the foundation area and surrounding slope. The event interrupted a major motorway connection in Sicily without causing fatalities or injuries.

Total collapse of a national road bridge over the Trebbia river near Bobbio (Piacenza, Emilia-Romagna) on 14 September 2015, triggered by the severe flooding of the Trebbia during intense late-summer rainfall. The Trebbia is known for its powerful flash floods in the upper valley. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The medieval Ponte Gobbo (humpback bridge), a symbol of Bobbio, survived the event despite heavy flooding around it; the collapsed structure was a modern RC road bridge. Il ponte di Barberino (arco in muratura anni '50) cedette per la spinta dell'acqua durante la piena 'cinquecentenaria' del Trebbia; fonti locali segnalano anche il degrado manutentivo pregresso del manufatto. Nessuna perizia pubblica reperita. [Il database Polimi (D'Angelo et al. 2025, S3, record P080, dec=1) classifica invece il processo come: erosione verticale (scour).]

The masonry pillar was swept away by the Tammarecchia river in full spate, isolating the Alto Tammaro area and cutting off several communities. One of 5 bridges in Circello alone destroyed in the event. The Esercito Italiano deployed Bailey bridge technology; a provisional crossing was installed within months. A permanent replacement bridge (€950,000) was inaugurated in 2018. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse. Multi-span reinforced-concrete bridge (RC piers and abutments, RC deck) with piers in the riverbed; collapse triggered by failure of a central pier due to foundation scour during the flood.

The Allaro river overwhelmed the bridge, causing the collapse of the 'ponte monarchico' (the older of the two parallel structures). The remaining partial structure was demolished on 6 November 2015 for safety reasons. ANAS appaltò reconstruction works of €2.5 million in December 2016; the new bridge was opened in December 2020. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific bridge collapse (though the broader flood claimed multiple victims in the area). Piena della fiumara Allaro (alluvione Locride, nov. 2015): crollo della corsia 'monarchica' del ponte SS106. Il successivo progressivo abbassamento dell'impalcato della corsia superstite durante le piene seguenti indica cedimenti fondali (scalzamento) come meccanismo probabile; nessuna perizia pubblica reperita.

Partial collapse of the Viadotto Marrazzita on the SP2 'Saurina' at km 4+100 near Stigliano (Matera, Basilicata) on 18 March 2016, caused by intense rainfall that saturated the roadway embankment and caused the voiding of material around a bridge abutment, opening a large sinkhole. The Vigili del fuoco and Protezione Civile intervened with pumps. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The structure had been closed to traffic since the 2015 event. No fatalities or injuries were reported as the bridge was already interdicted. The 2016 collapse was total, completing the destruction begun a year earlier. Provincial technicians immediately began precautionary checks on an adjacent bridge. The Bormida flood sheared off the bridge span, isolating approximately 40 families in the borgate Conradi and Pallareto. The mayor declared the situation 'dramatic'; a temporary ford was installed as an emergency measure. The event prompted significant debate on bridge hydraulic design standards, as the old bridge had zero freeboard against the 200-year flood. A new 57-metre single-span steel bridge was inaugurated in October 2021 after €1.76 million of Regione Liguria funding. Documentazione Regione Liguria (ricostruzione): il vecchio ponte aveva franco idraulico nullo rispetto alla piena bicentennale e pile in alveo con rischio di ostruzione al deflusso; la piena del Bormida ha tranciato la campata. Il nuovo ponte elimina tali criticita' (campata unica, franco 1,5 m). [Il database Polimi (D'Angelo et al. 2025, S3, record P127, dec=1) classifica invece il processo come: erosione laterale di sponda + carico idraulico sulla struttura.]

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Rio Bevera near Monesi di Triora (Imperia, Liguria) on 24 November 2016, triggered by a landslide associated with the extreme rainfall event that struck the Liguria di Ponente — particularly the Valle Arroscia and upper Val Bormida areas, where accumulations reached 349 mm in 24 hours at Pieve di Teco. The Monesi di Triora area is in the upper Tanaro basin and was severely affected by the event. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Partial collapse of a municipal bridge over the Tanaro river near Priola (Cuneo, Piemonte) on 25 November 2016, triggered by the extreme flooding of the upper Tanaro during the major November 2016 Piemonte flood event. Tanaro levels at Garessio reached 4.88 metres, described as comparable to the catastrophic 1994 alluvione. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P125 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = spalle, rilevato di accesso; evidenza di sormonto = yes.

Partial collapse of a second road bridge over the Po river at Sanfront (Cuneo) during the 24 November 2016 flood, distinct from event B16.11.03 (~0.8 km apart). Documented in the Polimi river-bridge failure database (record P144, dec=1): lateral bank erosion affecting the approach embankment. D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', IJDRR, database supplementare S3, record P144 (dec=1): secondo ponte danneggiato a Sanfront nella piena del Po del 24/11/2016 (a ~800 m dal ponte della scheda B16.11.03); processo = erosione laterale di sponda; componente = rilevato di accesso; sormonto = no.

Partial collapse of the Ponte Allaro on the SS106 Jonica national road near Caulonia Marina (Reggio Calabria, Calabria) on 23 January 2017, during a severe rainfall event that caused the Allaro river to flood. Two bridge spans on the carriageway already closed to traffic since the November 2015 flood (which had caused partial collapse of the original 'monarchico' bridge) gave way completely. ANAS had already contracted reconstruction works worth 2.5 million euros in December 2016. The SS106 remained closed in both directions. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The new bridge was finally rebuilt and reopened in December 2020 after five years of closures. Anas e Ministero dell'Interno documentano l'avvallamento del piano viabile e l'abbassamento dell'impalcato della corsia 'repubblicana' del ponte Allaro a seguito delle piene: cedimento fondale progressivo (scalzamento) che porto' a chiusura e successiva demolizione del manufatto.

Total collapse of bridge no. 167 on the A14 motorway at km 235+800 near Camerano (Ancona, Marche) on 9 March 2017 at approximately 13:30, during lifting operations as part of the construction of a third motorway lane. The temporary support structure failed, causing the bridge span to fall onto the open motorway carriageway below. Two people died — Emidio Diomede (60) and Antonella Viviani (54) from Spinetoli (Ascoli Piceno) — whose car was crushed by the falling deck while travelling towards the hospital; three Romanian construction workers were injured. The judicial investigation involved 22 individuals and four companies (Autostrade per l'Italia, Spea Engineering, Pavimental and Delabech), with charges of culpable homicide, culpable collapse and workplace safety violations. The MIT appointed an independent inspection commission. The engineering expert appointed by the prosecution concluded that risks had been systematically underestimated in both the design and execution phases.

Total collapse of the Marene ramp of the Fossano ring road (SS231) on 18 April 2017. The span failed suddenly without a significant external load; two Carabinieri escaped immediately before the collapse. Initial ANAS technical assessments pointed to construction defects as the leading cause hypothesis. The governing physical failure process has not been established in publicly available documentation and remains Unspecified.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Chiusella stream near Strambino (Torino, Piemonte) on 15 June 2017, caused by hydraulic forces during a flood event. The Chiusella and its confluence with the Dora Baltea near Strambino is a recurrently flood-prone area with a documented history of bridge and infrastructure damage. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P181 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione verticale (scour); componenti danneggiate = pile, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Total collapse of the municipal bridge at the mouth of the Chioma stream near Quercianella (Livorno, Tuscany) on 10 September 2017, triggered by the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Livorno area — causing 8 deaths and destroying multiple bridges and infrastructure after 250 mm of rain fell in approximately 2 hours. The Chioma stream, normally reduced to a rivulet in summer, overflowed dramatically and destroyed the bridge connecting the road to the Chioma Beach residence and marina, isolating residents. A rescue operation was mounted by the Vigili del fuoco and Protezione Civile. The bridge was rebuilt by the Comune di Rosignano Marittimo within approximately 7 months and reopened in June 2018. Rapporto IRPI-CNR (Polaris): la furia delle acque del Chioma fece letteralmente saltare/sradico' il ponte alla foce durante la flash flood; il ponte ricostruito e' issabile proprio per garantire il deflusso in piena (Regione Toscana).

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Rio Maggiore in the Limoncino locality of Livorno (Tuscany) on 10 September 2017, triggered by the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Livorno area. The Rio Maggiore, partially culverted through the city, overflowed catastrophically and destroyed the bridge on the road connecting Limoncino to Valle Benedetta, isolating hillside residential areas. The Regione Toscana, in collaboration with RFI (Rete Ferroviaria Italiana), rebuilt the bridge in approximately two weeks using railway bridge technology, reopening it on 26 September 2017 — one of the fastest bridge reconstructions ever recorded in Italy after a flood. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P120 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=0.5): processo = erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = spalle, rilevato di accesso, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Total collapse of the Ponte Stefano Gioia over the Lao river near Laino Castello (Cosenza, Calabria) on 7 December 2017 at approximately 14:45. The bridge, a 70-metre glued laminated timber (glulam) structure built in 2000 by the Consorzio di Bonifica del Pollino and considered innovative at the time of its inauguration, had been closed to traffic since October 2017 due to detected structural deterioration. The collapse was attributed to complete lack of maintenance since construction, with fungal growth and wood rot having weakened the primary structural elements. The bridge connected the Campicello fraction of Laino Castello with the Nuppolara contrada of Papasidero near the Grotta del Romito, and was named after a rafting guide from Laino Borgo who died in Chile in 2010. No fatalities or injuries were reported as the structure was already closed.

Partial collapse (severe structural damage requiring full demolition and rebuilding) of the SP 24 overpass connecting Montirone and Poncarale over the A21 motorway near Brescia (Lombardy) on 2 January 2018, caused by a catastrophic fire ignited when a fuel tanker exploded following a chain-collision on the A21 below the bridge. Temperatures reaching 600°C severely damaged the RC beams of the entire bridge span. Six people died in the road accident itself. Structural surveys revealed concrete cores were irreparably compromised; the overpass was demolished in April 2018 and fully rebuilt by Autovia Padana, reopening in September 2019 after over 20 months of closure.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Montone river in Forlì (Emilia-Romagna) on 2 February 2018, caused by hydraulic forces during a flood event. The Montone river, which runs through the Forlì urban park area, has a history of flooding events that have caused repeated infrastructure damage. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P117 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = carico idraulico sulla struttura; componenti danneggiate = pile, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = si.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Mazaro dry riverbed near Salemi (Trapani, Sicily) on 8 February 2018, triggered by exceptional rainfall that caused the normally dry Mazaro riverbed to fill rapidly. Winter storms in western Sicily in February 2018 caused widespread hydraulic damage. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P093 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=0.5): processo = erosione verticale (scour) + carico idraulico sulla struttura; componenti danneggiate = impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no. Nota: discrepanza di coordinate tra i due database, abbinamento per data con candidato unico.

Total collapse of the Polcevera Viaduct (Morandi Bridge) in Genoa on 14 August 2018, involving multiple spans and causing 43 fatalities and 11 injuries. The collapse occurred without a clearly identifiable external trigger and is generally associated with structural deterioration and maintenance-related deficiencies.

Total collapse of an overpass along the A14 motorway interchange in Bologna on 6 August 2018 following a tanker truck explosion and intense fire. The collapse caused severe disruption to the motorway network. Casualties associated with the explosion event are not directly attributed to the structural collapse in the present database.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Rio Coccodi near Uta (Cagliari, Sardinia) on 10 October 2018, triggered by the extreme flood that struck the Cagliari hinterland following 250 mm of rainfall in 24 hours. The same event caused the collapse of the SS195 bridge at Capoterra and forced the evacuation of 49 residents from Uta. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P174 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione verticale (scour); componenti danneggiate = pile, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Partial collapse of the bridge over the Rio Santa Lucia on the SS195 Sulcitana national road connecting Cagliari to Capoterra and Pula (Sardinia) on 10 October 2018 at approximately 17:30, triggered by the overflow of the Rio Santa Lucia during an extreme rainfall event (250 mm/24h at Capoterra, half the annual average). ANAS had closed the SS195 in the hours prior to the collapse due to a large sinkhole that had opened at the Rumianca jetty area. The collapse cut the national road in two, isolating the Capoterra area. Capoterra was already known for a deadly 2008 flood. The broader event caused 1 fatality and the evacuation of 57 residents from the area. No injuries directly attributed to this specific collapse. Esondazione del Rio Santa Lucia con rottura degli argini: le acque scalzarono la sede stradale e la corrente asporto' un tratto del ponte, tagliando in due la SS195 (fonti ANSA/stampa nazionale).

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Fersina stream near Fierozzo (Trento, Trentino-Alto Adige) on 28-29 October 2018, triggered by the extreme hydraulic loading of the Tempesta Vaia storm system that struck northeastern Italy with record rainfall and wind gusts exceeding 200 km/h. The Fersina valley was severely affected by flooding and landslides during the storm. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P121 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=0.5): processo = carico idraulico sulla struttura; componenti danneggiate = impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = yes.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Rio Piazzina near Stramentizzo (Trento, Trentino-Alto Adige) on 29 October 2018, caused by the extreme hydraulic forces generated by Tempesta Vaia. The Rio Piazzina, a minor tributary in the Val di Fiemme area, was overwhelmed by the record rainfall associated with the storm. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P118 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = carico idraulico sulla struttura; componenti danneggiate = rilevato di accesso, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = yes.

Partial collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Degano stream near Comeglians (Udine, Friuli-Venezia Giulia) on 29-30 October 2018, caused by the Tempesta Vaia storm system. The Carnia region, including Comeglians, was among the most severely affected areas in Friuli, with seven people evacuated and the entire area losing electricity for several days. The Degano river and its tributaries overflowed, damaging or destroying multiple infrastructure elements. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse. Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Adda river at Pizzighettone (Cremona, Lombardy) on 30 October 2018, caused by the extreme flooding of the Adda river during the Tempesta Vaia event and its downstream hydrological consequences. The Adda reached exceptionally high levels as snowmelt and intense rainfall from the Alpine catchment propagated downstream. The cycle-pedestrian bridge, which connected the historic walled town of Pizzighettone across the river, was swept away by the floodwaters. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Per almeno due giorni un'enorme massa di alberi, tronchi e ramaglie trasportata dalla piena dell'Adda si accumulo' sotto i piloni della passerella; il 30/10/2018 alle 8:35 la pressione dell''isola galleggiante' di detriti fece cedere le pile centrali (fonti locali e AIPo). [Il database Polimi (D'Angelo et al. 2025, S3, record P096, dec=1) classifica invece il processo come: carico idraulico sulla struttura.]

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Aviso stream near Cavalese (Trento, Trentino-Alto Adige) on 29-30 October 2018, caused by the Tempesta Vaia storm system. Cavalese, in the Val di Fiemme, was one of the most severely affected municipalities in Trentino during Vaia: the Aviso torrent and its tributaries overwhelmed their banks, destroying infrastructure and isolating communities. The broader Vaia event caused 2 deaths in Trentino and over 500 evacuations across the province. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P145 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione verticale (scour); componenti danneggiate = pile, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Partial collapse (severe structural damage requiring full demolition and rebuilding) of the overpass on the SP 32 Novedratese at km 8.890 in Carimate (Como, Lombardy) on 18 March 2019, caused by the impact of a heavy goods vehicle transporting an excavator with an oversized load that struck the intrados of the bridge while travelling on the underlying via dei Giovi. All RC carrying beams were damaged, with rebar severed along the entire span. The Provincia di Como ordered the immediate total closure of the Novedratese for a minimum of three months and proceeded with demolition and full reconstruction of the bridge deck. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The closure caused severe traffic disruption across the Canturino and Brianza areas for several months.

Total collapse of the bridge over the Rio Albedosa on the SP 155 (Pratalborato fraction of Capriata d'Orba, Alessandria, Piemonte) during the night of 21-22 October 2019, triggered by an extreme flood following record rainfall (425 mm/24h at Gavi, the highest in 100 years). One fatality was recorded: Fabrizio Torre, 52, a transport driver from Sale, whose vehicle was swept away by floodwaters near the collapsed bridge. His passenger, a Brazilian national, survived by clinging to a tree. The SP 155 — a key link between Novi Ligure and Ovada — remained closed for several months pending construction of a provisional Bailey bridge, which reopened in February 2020. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P134 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=0.5): processo = erosione verticale (scour) + erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = spalle, rilevato di accesso, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Total collapse of the northbound carriageway of the Viadotto Madonna del Monte on the A6 Torino-Savona motorway near Savona (Liguria) on 24 November 2019 at approximately 14:05, caused by a landslide of over 15,000 m³ that detached from an adjacent hillside not classified as at-risk in the regional hydrogeological risk maps and struck a bridge pillar, bringing down approximately 20-40 metres of bridge deck. A tragedy was narrowly averted when security guard Daniele Cassol stopped oncoming traffic — including a bus — on the brink of the collapsed section. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The bridge was rebuilt in an extraordinary 88 days by Autostrada dei Fiori and reopened in February 2020, becoming a symbol of rapid infrastructure recovery.

Total collapse of a pedestrian bridge over the Sarno river on via Ripuaria in Castellammare di Stabia (Naples, Campania) on 21 December 2019, triggered by the overflow of the Sarno river during severe rainfall. The bridge, which had reportedly been out of use for some years, was destroyed by the rising river; debris from the collapsed structure threatened to block the river flow. The Campania Protezione Civile confirmed no injuries. Municipal technical staff and the Consorzio Bacino del Sarno were alerted and the Genio Civile coordinated the emergency response. Il Sarno ruppe gli argini in via Ripuaria (22/12/2019) e la piena travolse la passerella pedonale dismessa; le macerie in alveo crearono poi un effetto diga, rimosso dal Genio Civile nel gennaio 2020.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge near Gonessa (Sud Sardegna, Sardinia) in April 2020, triggered by overload from a heavy vehicle exceeding the structural load capacity of the bridge. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The structure was a small municipal crossing typical of the rural Sardinian road network.

Total collapse of the Ponte Emilio Barsanti at Albiano Magra on 8 April 2020. Court-appointed expert findings reported during the subsequent proceedings identified long-term movement of a pre-existing landslide/paleolandslide affecting the bridge alignment as a principal collapse factor, with construction/reconstruction and monitoring issues also considered contributing. Classified as Landslide; the detailed structural failure process remains general.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Paglia river near Abbadia San Salvatore (Siena, Tuscany) in May 2020, triggered by hydraulic phenomena following intense rainfall. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P184 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione verticale (scour); componenti danneggiate = pile, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Arrone stream near Santa Maria di Galeria (Rome, Lazio) in September 2020, triggered by overload from a heavy vehicle that exceeded the load capacity of the structure. One injury was reported. The collapse interrupted local road connections in the area northwest of Rome.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Niel stream near Gaby (Aosta, Valle d'Aosta) on 2-3 October 2020, triggered by the extreme flash flood that struck northwestern Italy with record rainfall exceeding 600 mm in 24 hours in some locations. The collapse was explicitly reported by the Valle d'Aosta civil protection authorities during the emergency, isolating the Gaby area. No fatalities directly attributed to this specific collapse. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P154 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=0.5): processo = erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = rilevato di accesso, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Cervaro stream near Piedicavallo (Biella, Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020, during the catastrophic flood that broke historical rainfall records in Piemonte (610 mm/24h recorded at Piedicavallo itself). No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P155 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=0.5): processo = carico idraulico sulla struttura; componenti danneggiate = pile, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = si.

Partial collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Strona stream near Crevacuore (Biella, Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020, caused by the extreme hydraulic loading associated with the October 2020 northwestern Italy flood event. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Rapporto ARPA Piemonte 'Evento del 2-3 ottobre 2020' (rev 1.1, 14/10/2020, p. 80): nelle valli Sessera e Mosso i processi principali si svilupparono a carico dei corsi d'acqua principali e dei rii secondari, con tracimazioni ed erosioni spondali diffuse e danni alla viabilità nei comuni di Pray, Coggiola e Crevacuore; la Fig. 77 documenta i danni a Crevacuore sul T. Strona di Postua (zona ex cartiera). Il crollo parziale del ponte non è descritto singolarmente nel rapporto: l'attribuzione del processo (erosione spondale/tracimazione) al manufatto è inferita dal contesto documentato nel comune sul medesimo corso d'acqua — associazione da confermare, quindi evidenza 'Probable'.

Total collapse of Ponte Lenzino on the SS45 over the Trebbia on 3 October 2020. Early prosecution hypotheses focused on foundation scour, but the 2026 GUP decision, relying on court-expert evidence, attributed the collapse to movement of the Carisasca landslide acting on the Genoa-side abutment and rejected river erosion as the governing cause. Classified here as Landslide; the detailed structural process is retained as Other documented mode.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Sesia river connecting Romagnano Sesia and Gattinara (Novara, Piemonte) on 3 October 2020. The bridge had been closed overnight as a precaution, was briefly reopened when conditions appeared to improve, then collapsed at approximately 13:30 — the collapse was broadcast in near-real time during a Facebook live session by the two mayors. One person died in the Sesia river floods nearby, but not directly from this collapse. The event was widely reported nationally. Rapporto ARPA Piemonte 'Evento del 2-3 ottobre 2020' (rev 1.1, 14/10/2020, pp. 69-75): il ponte tra Gattinara e Romagnano crollò il 3 ottobre per il cedimento di una pila; il rapporto inquadra il collasso tra le gravi ripercussioni dell'erosione del fondo alveo sulle opere, in un tratto in cui le passate estrazioni di inerti hanno prodotto un abbassamento del fondo di circa 2 m dagli anni '70 con progressiva riduzione della sezione (Fig. 56); la mappatura Copernicus EMS segnala il ponte sulla SP142 seriamente danneggiato (Fig. 41). Contesto: colmi mai registrati sul Sesia (Borgosesia oltre 4 m sopra il livello di pericolo, portata >3000 mc/s). Nota temporale: il rapporto colloca il crollo nella mattina del 3/10, mentre le cronache lo riprendono alle 13:30-13:45 circa, dopo chiusura precauzionale la sera del 2/10 e riapertura alle 12:30.

Total collapse of the Ponte Manfredi over the Arroscia stream near Vessalico (Imperia, Liguria) during the October 2020 flood event affecting the Ponente Ligure. The collapse was explicitly named in national media coverage of the disaster. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P159 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = altro processo (es. colata detritica/frana); componenti danneggiate = impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = yes.

Total/functional collapse of Bagnasco's historic 'ponte romano' during the October 2020 Tanaro flood. Contemporary sources explicitly record the collapse; the official ARPA event report documents overtopping and damage to the upper arches, supporting overtopping/hydrodynamic action as the governing process. The affected component is retained as Deck / superstructure.

Total collapse of the Passerella Squarciafichi cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Roia river in Ventimiglia (Imperia, Liguria) on 2-3 October 2020, caused by the extreme flooding of the Roia river during the October 2020 Ponente Ligure flood event. The structure was described as a symbol of the city. No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse. S3, record P162 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=0.5): processo = erosione verticale (scour); componenti danneggiate = pile, spalle, rilevato di accesso, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Gesso stream near Valdieri (Cuneo, Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020, caused by the extreme hydraulic loading during the record-breaking October 2020 flood event in the Cuneo Alps. Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Strona stream near Valstrona (Verbania, Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020, triggered by the extreme flood affecting the Verbano-Cusio-Ossola area where rainfall records were broken (630 mm/24h at Sambughetto). No fatalities directly attributed to this collapse. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P186 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione verticale (scour); componenti danneggiate = spalle, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian wooden overpass on via Laurentina near Piazzale Ardigò in Rome (Lazio) on 8 October 2020, caused by a crane truck that accidentally struck the underside of the timber bridge while manoeuvring on the road below, splitting the structure in two. The bridge was unoccupied at the time and no injuries were reported. Roma Capitale coordinated restoration works, with the missing span reinstalled in 2021.

Partial collapse of a municipal bridge over the Mollarino stream near Picinisco (Frosinone, Lazio) on 19 October 2020, triggered by hydraulic phenomena. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P164 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = rilevato di accesso; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Total collapse (washout) of one of three bridges over the Pianale stream between the hamlets of Camasco and Corte e Costa in Varallo (Vercelli, Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020, during the record-breaking Sesia basin flood. The three bridges were washed away by the flood of the Pianale stream and Nono torrent, in a sector where the ARPA Piemonte event report describes hyperconcentrated flows and debris flows along the entire minor network. The three collapses are documented collectively in the report (see B20.10.14-B20.10.16); structural details are not available. No fatalities attributed to these collapses. Rapporto ARPA Piemonte 'Evento del 2-3 ottobre 2020' (rev 1.1, 14/10/2020, p. 70, Fig. 57b e 58): la piena del Rio Pianale e del T. Nono provoco' l'asportazione di tre ponti sul rio Pianale tra Camasco e la frazione Corte e Costa (comune di Varallo). Il rapporto inquadra i processi sui tributari del medio-basso Sesia come trasporto iperconcentrato (piene con elevato trasporto di fondo) e colate detritiche lungo tutto il reticolato minore, con effetti parossistici proprio sui torrenti Nono e Mastallone (p. 69): l'attribuzione 'Debris flow / solid transport' e' inferita da questo contesto documentato, non dichiarata per il singolo manufatto - evidenza 'Probable'. Total collapse (complete washout) of the footbridge over the Sesia river at Campertogno (Vercelli, Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020. Bank erosion by the Sesia river, which reached unprecedented levels throughout the basin (5.2 m peak at Campertogno vs a 4.0 m danger threshold), damaged the road to the local campsite and completely removed the footbridge, as documented by the ARPA Piemonte event report. No fatalities attributed to this collapse. Rapporto ARPA Piemonte 'Evento del 2-3 ottobre 2020' (rev 1.1, 14/10/2020, p. 71, Fig. 59): a Campertogno l'erosione di sponda ad opera del Sesia causo' danni alla via di collegamento al campeggio e l'asportazione completa della passerella sul torrente. Meccanismo (erosione spondale) e distruzione completa del manufatto documentati dalla didascalia del rapporto: evidenza 'Documented'. Contesto: colmi mai registrati sul Sesia da monte a valle (a Campertogno colmo 5,2 m alle 03:30 UTC del 3/10 contro livello di pericolo 4,0 m, Tab. 5). Tipologia strutturale e materiale non desumibili dal rapporto; coordinate approssimate (zona campeggio di Campertogno, exact_location FALSE).

Total collapse (complete washout) of the bridge at loc. Barchi in Ormea (Cuneo, Piemonte) over the Tanaro river on 2-3 October 2020. The bridge, rebuilt after the November 1994 flood, was completely washed away by the Tanaro flood, which exceeded the 2016 historical reference levels in the upper valley (estimated return period >200 years). Documented by the ARPA Piemonte event report. No fatalities attributed to this collapse. Rapporto ARPA Piemonte 'Evento del 2-3 ottobre 2020' (rev 1.1, 14/10/2020, p. 93, Fig. 100): a Ormea, loc. Barchi, il ponte - ricostruito dopo l'alluvione del 1994 - fu completamente asportato dalla piena del Tanaro. Il crollo e la causa idraulica sono quindi documentati da fonte tecnica, ma il meccanismo di dettaglio non e' specificato; per l'alta Val Tanaro il rapporto indica in generale numerosi ponti gravemente danneggiati o abbattuti 'sia per l'erosione delle spalle sia per il sormonto delle acque in piena' (p. 92), senza attribuzione al singolo manufatto: processo ed evidenza restano 'Unspecified'. Contesto idrometrico: a Ponte di Nava e Garessio superati i riferimenti storici del 2016, TR stimato >200 anni (Tab. 6). Coordinate approssimate (concentrico di Ormea, exact_location FALSE).

Partial collapse of the bridge providing access to the Vallone di Monte Colombo just downstream of San Giacomo di Entracque (Cuneo, Piemonte) on 2-3 October 2020: left-bank erosion by the Gesso della Barra torrent, in violent flood, removed the bridge abutment. The valley road was also washed away for stretches of hundreds of metres, isolating the hamlet of San Giacomo. Documented by the ARPA Piemonte event report. No fatalities or injuries reported. Rapporto ARPA Piemonte 'Evento del 2-3 ottobre 2020' (rev 1.1, 14/10/2020, p. 89, Fig. 93a): subito a valle di San Giacomo di Entracque, lungo il Gesso della Barra, un'erosione della sponda sinistra asporto' la spalla del ponte utilizzato per accedere al Vallone di Monte Colombo. Meccanismo (erosione spondale) e componente coinvolta (spalla) esplicitamente documentati: evidenza 'Documented'; crollo parziale (PC). Contesto: violenta attivita' torrentizia lungo il T. Gesso della Barra con asportazione della strada del vallone per tratti di centinaia di metri e isolamento di San Giacomo (p. 89, Fig. 92). Tipologia strutturale e materiale non desumibili; coordinate approssimate (zona San Giacomo di Entracque, exact_location FALSE).

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Enel hydroelectric canal near Pallanzeno (Verbania, Piemonte) on 6 November 2020, triggered by the transit of a heavily loaded truck transporting cleaning material for the Rio Valmaggia. The structure may have been weakened by the October 2020 flood. The truck remained suspended on the collapsed bridge overnight; the driver was unharmed. Enel, owner of the canal, undertook reconstruction of a new permanent bridge inaugurated in 2024.

Partial collapse of a national bridge over the Neto river near Crotone (Calabria) in November 2020, triggered by hydraulic phenomena following intense rainfall. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P172 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione verticale (scour); componenti danneggiate = non specificate; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Iornito stream near Melissa (Crotone, Calabria) in November 2020, triggered by hydraulic phenomena. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P173 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione del rilevato in alveo/golena; componenti danneggiate = spalle, rilevato di accesso, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Partial collapse of a provincial/regional bridge over the Rio de Malò near Bitti (Nuoro, Sardinia) in November 2020, triggered by hydraulic phenomena associated with severe rainfall affecting central Sardinia. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge over the Mis stream near Gosaldo (Belluno, Veneto) in December 2020, triggered by hydraulic phenomena. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Gosaldo sustained two bridge collapses simultaneously during the same hydraulic event. Total collapse of a second municipal bridge over the Mis stream near Gosaldo (Belluno, Veneto) in December 2020, triggered by the same hydraulic event that caused the simultaneous collapse of the cycle-pedestrian bridge in the same municipality. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Piena documentata; meccanismo di dettaglio non ricostruibile dalle fonti disponibili.

Total collapse of the bascule bridge (ponte levatoio) at the Darsena di Pagliari in La Spezia (Liguria) on 12 May 2021, during a closing manoeuvre after allowing a vessel to exit the marina. The collapse is attributed to the failure of one of the hydraulic pistons responsible for lowering the bridge deck. The structure, inaugurated in 2010 by the Port Authority at a cost of over 9 million euros as part of the Pagliari marina development, was 21 metres long with a 14-metre mast. No fatalities or injuries were reported, as the area is routinely closed to traffic during bridge operations. The Port Authority immediately sequestered the structure for judicial investigation for alleged culpable collapse.

Total collapse of the bridge over the Logonovo canal along via della Salina near Comacchio (Ferrara, Emilia-Romagna) on 28 August 2021, due to structural deterioration. Municipal technical staff had carried out an inspection the previous day and immediately closed the structure after detecting signs of imminent failure; the bridge collapsed the following morning. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The collapse isolated the historic Saline di Comacchio — an important tourist and ecological site — and disrupted local mussel farming operations for over a year while reconstruction was planned.

Total collapse of a lateral service gallery of the Ponte dell'Industria (Ponte di Ferro) over the Tevere river in Rome on the night of 2-3 October 2021, triggered by a large fire that started from makeshift encampments beneath the bridge and spread to gas and electrical service conduits running along the structure. A lateral pedestrian and utility gallery approximately 50 metres long collapsed into the river; the main vehicular deck, though severely damaged, did not collapse. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The bridge, built in 1863 and an important connection between the Ostiense and Marconi districts, was reopened to vehicles on 12 December 2021 following emergency repairs.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Quazzola stream in via Tecci near Quiliano (Savona, Liguria) on 4 October 2021, triggered by the extreme flash flood that struck the Savona hinterland during a severe rainfall event. The structure connected two residential properties across the stream and its collapse left two families isolated. The event occurred during a major flood that also caused the overflow of the Erro and Letimbro rivers and widespread infrastructure damage across the Savona province. Total collapse of the Ponte San Bartolomeo on the SS187 state road near Alcamo Marina (Trapani, Sicily) on the night of 10-11 December 2021, triggered by the failure of the central pillar following extreme flooding of the San Bartolomeo river during heavy rainfall in western Sicily. The structure, already known to be in deteriorating condition and previously subject to emergency works in 2019, collapsed while a vehicle was approaching and narrowly avoided being swept away. No fatalities or injuries were reported. The SS187 was closed immediately; ANAS and the Sicilian Region coordinated provisional replacement works. Cedimento della pila centrale per scalzamento durante la piena del San Bartolomeo; caso citato dalla letteratura tecnica (FABRE 2022).

Total collapse of Ponte Guastacconcio over the Sangro on 13 February 2022 after prior closure for progressive settlement of the central pier. Parliamentary records link the pre-collapse deformation to repeated Sangro floods and riverbed lowering; D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), record P192, classifies vertical erosion/scour. The final collapse occurred without a discrete flood at the time, so triggered remains FALSE.

Partial collapse of the Via Volturno overpass over the western ring road (tangenziale Ovest) in Brescia on 24 August 2022, caused by the impact of a heavy goods vehicle transporting a crane whose boom struck the underside of the bridge deck. Five reinforced concrete beams were destroyed in the impact. The structure, one of the most heavily trafficked crossings in the city with approximately 80,000 vehicles per day, was closed immediately and the city traffic network was severely disrupted. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Temporary shoring works involving 250 props were installed and load tests were carried out before partial reopening.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge over the Misa river near Arcevia (Ancona, Marche) on 15 September 2022, triggered by the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Marche region. The bridge was destroyed by the extreme hydraulic forces associated with the Misa river in full spate following exceptional rainfall exceeding 400 mm in a few hours in the Cantiano area. Cantiano was the epicentre of the flood event, recording over 419 mm of rainfall in a few hours — a record for the Marche region — which caused total destruction of local infrastructure including roads, bridges and buildings. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. Partial collapse of the Cavalcavia XXV Aprile in Novara (Piemonte) on 9 October 2022, involving the detachment of a retaining wall section. The structure, which had shown signs of foundation deterioration since at least 2013 and had been subject to emergency consolidation works in 2015, was not among the bridges flagged as high-risk by the municipal authorities. The carriageway had already been reduced to two lanes. One vehicle was involved but no serious injuries were reported. The event prompted immediate closure and renewed debate on bridge maintenance across the city.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge on the Paraturo stream near Laino Castello (Cosenza, Calabria) on 17 November 2022, triggered by intense rainfall and consequent hydraulic loading. The structure, built approximately 30 years earlier by the Consorzio di Bonifica del Pollino in reinforced concrete, connected the Calabrian municipality to Rotonda (Basilicata). No fatalities or injuries were reported, but residents were left isolated following the collapse. Piena documentata; meccanismo di dettaglio non ricostruibile dalle fonti disponibili.

Partial collapse of a municipal overpass in via Vignetta near Varazze (Savona, Liguria) on 25 November 2022, caused by the impact of a heavy goods vehicle transporting an excavator that struck the underside of the bridge deck while travelling on the A10 motorway below. The structure suffered irreparable damage and was subsequently demolished. No fatalities or injuries were reported. A provisional Bailey bridge was installed within one week to restore access to approximately 40 residents who had been cut off.

Total collapse of a provincial/regional bridge on the SP329 near Monteverdi Marittimo (Pisa, Tuscany) on the night of 1 December 2022, caused by the sudden failure of a pillar. The structure connected the town centre to the hamlet of Canneto. No fatalities or injuries were reported; the collapse occurred at night with no vehicles in transit. The road remained closed for several months while a temporary Bailey bridge was installed.

Partial collapse of Ponte Termini near Terme Vigliatore (Sicily) on 3 December 2022 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with intense flooding of the Mazzarà stream during an extreme rainfall event. No fatalities or injuries were reported Piena documentata; meccanismo di dettaglio non ricostruibile dalle fonti disponibili.

Total collapse of Ponte Tredici Luci near Chiusa Sclafani (Sicily) on 16 December 2022 caused by progressive long-term structural deterioration associated with water infiltration through the deteriorated bridge deck waterproofing system. The prolonged infiltration process led to internal damage and eventual collapse of two masonry arches. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the Collerenti bridge over the Salinello between Bellante and Sant'Omero on 29 December 2022, initiated by failure of the Bellante-side abutment. Initial inspections considered overload, but court-appointed experts later identified a construction defect as the predominant predisposing factor, with rainfall-related erosion and heavy-vehicle traffic as contributing/accelerating factors. No vehicle was crossing at the instant of failure; no discrete trigger is assigned.

Total collapse of the bridge at Molina Aterno (Abruzzo) on 18 January 2023 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with intense flooding and scour processes affecting the Aterno river. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Processi di scour sull'Aterno indicati dalle fonti dell'evento.
Partial collapse of Ponte di Promano near Città di Castello (Umbria) on 30 January 2023 following impact from an overheight heavy vehicle. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the Ortiano II bridge near Longobucco (Calabria) on 3 May 2023 following extreme hydraulic and scour phenomena affecting the Trionto river during severe flooding. The collapse occurred shortly after the bridge opening and did not cause fatalities or injuries. D'Angelo et al. (2025), Structure and Infrastructure Engineering, case study con sopralluogo degli autori: crollo della terza campata del viadotto Ortiano II (SS177, 7 campate x30 m, in esercizio dal 2016) alle ~18:00 del 03/05/2023 per scalzamento della fondazione della pila 3: pile prive di fondazioni profonde (plinti 8,70x7,40x2,00 m su rilevato in massi), plinti gia' parzialmente scoperti da piene precedenti (foto dal 2021); un affioramento roccioso in destra deviava la corrente verso le pile 3 e 4 con vortici e scavo dell'alveo; moto roto-traslazionale della pila verso l'alveo e caduta dell'impalcato in semplice appoggio. Ponte chiuso al traffico ~1 ora prima del crollo: nessuna vittima.

Total collapse of a provincial bridge near San Martino in Argine (Emilia-Romagna) on 17 May 2023 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with extreme flooding of the Idice stream during the 2023 Emilia-Romagna flood event. No fatalities or injuries were reported. D'Angelo et al. (2025), Structure and Infrastructure Engineering, case study con sopralluogo degli autori: rottura dell'argine destro dell'Idice ~700 m a valle del ponte della Motta (breccia >100 m, poco dopo mezzanotte del 16/05/2023) -> aumento della pendenza e della velocita' -> incisione generalizzata dell'alveo a monte stimata in ~4 m -> scalzamento dei corpi arginali; le spalle, immorsate negli argini e su fondazioni superficiali (a differenza delle pile su pali), collassarono trascinando due delle tre campate principali; la terza cadde poco dopo, verosimilmente per scalzamento delle pile residue (dati idrometro ARPAE sul ponte fino al collasso; ponte Gerber del 1958, 5 campate, ~100 m). [Il database Polimi (D'Angelo et al. 2025, S3, record P202, dec=1) classifica invece il processo come: erosione laterale di sponda.]

Total collapse of a provincial bridge in the Prada area near Ravenna (Emilia-Romagna) on 18 May 2023 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with extreme flooding during the 2023 Emilia-Romagna flood event. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P203 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=0.5): processo = erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = spalle, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = yes.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge in the Gambellara area of Ravenna (Emilia-Romagna) on 18 May 2023 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with extreme flooding of the Fosso Ghiaia canal during the 2023 Emilia-Romagna flood event. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P208 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = spalle, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = si.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge near Modigliana (Emilia-Romagna) on 19 May 2023 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with extreme rainfall and flooding of the Marzeno stream during the 2023 Emilia-Romagna flood event. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P204 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = spalle, rilevato di accesso, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge near Monterenzio (Emilia-Romagna) on 24 May 2023 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with extreme rainfall and flooding of the Sillaro river during the 2023 Emilia-Romagna flood event. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Database ponti fluviali danneggiati di D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), IJDRR 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', suppl. S3, record P205 (accuratezza diagnosi dec=1): processo = erosione verticale (scour); componenti danneggiate = pile, impalcato; evidenza di sormonto = no.

Total collapse of a road bridge over the Santerno river near Fontanelice (Bologna) during the May 2023 Emilia-Romagna floods. Event documented in the Polimi river-bridge failure database (record P206, dec=1); exact day within the 16-18 May 2023 event to be confirmed. D'Angelo, Ballio & Ravazzani (2025), 'Geomorphologic risk factors for river bridges', IJDRR, database supplementare S3, record P206 (dec=1): crollo totale di ponte stradale sul Santerno presso Fontanelice durante l'alluvione dell'Emilia-Romagna; processo = erosione verticale (scour) + erosione laterale di sponda; componenti danneggiate = impalcato e pile; sormonto = no. Giorno indicativo (evento 16-18/05/2023): data esatta da precisare.
Partial collapse of a provincial overpass near Coltano (Tuscany) on 27 July 2023 following impact from an overheight vehicle along the SP58 roadway. No fatalities or injuries were reported.

Total collapse of the new cycle-pedestrian footbridge at Borgo Rivola (Riolo Terme) during static load testing in September 2023. The structure failed under the water-tank test load; subsequent technical reporting by the designer discusses design errors and reconstruction. Classified as Design and Construction with Static load test trigger and Overstress process. The hydraulic record reported at the same location is not used to override this distinct load-test event.

Total collapse of a municipal bridge near Terenzo (Emilia-Romagna) on 30 October 2023 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with intense rainfall and flooding of the Sporzana stream. No fatalities or injuries were reported. Piena documentata; meccanismo di dettaglio non ricostruibile dalle fonti disponibili.

Total collapse of a cycle-pedestrian bridge near Vaiano (Tuscany) on 4 November 2023 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with intense rainfall and flooding of the Bisenzio river. Partial collapse (mechanical failure) of the movable lifting span of the Viadotto Navicelli on the FI-PI-LI expressway at Calambrone (Pisa/Livorno border) on 6 March 2026, caused by the sudden failure of one of the two steel hinges of the lifting mechanism. No hydraulic cause and no casualties (road and canal traffic were both interrupted for a routine lift at the time). Distinct from the 23 April 2014 event on the same bridge (B14.04.01). Project dates to 1990 (Italia '90 investment plan), tested/commissioned in 2004.

Total collapse of the SS16 bridge over the Trigno river near Montenero di Bisaccia (Molise) on 2 April 2026 following severe hydraulic phenomena associated with extreme flooding and scour processes affecting the riverbed during a major storm event. One person was reported missing following the collapse. Ipotesi tecnica prevalente: scalzamento di una pila in alveo durante la piena del Trigno; indagine della Procura di Larino in corso (2026).
